clue.text: Lager can adapted to hold husband's port

indicators.note: to hold means the rearranged letters take another piece inside them
adapted means altered into a new form, so the letters of lager can are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beer can modified to contain something belonging to a husband, namely his glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink to go with the husband's lager, but it is a harbour town. 'adapted' scrambles LAGERCAN to ARCANGEL, and 'to hold' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a seaport on the White Sea in northern Russia.

clue.text: Fellow with first letter reportedly securing cattle feed

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, so any fellow

indicators.note: reportedly signals the words are heard, not seen, so a spelling that sounds alike is used

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet; in the NATO alphabet it is spelt ALFA

explanation.surface: A man with the letter A, so to speak, holding onto animal fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, a leguminous plant, is grown widely as hay and fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Leader of crew supported by neat helmsman

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supported by another sits on top of it
the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from crew

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: The head of a rowing crew is propped up by a tidy steersman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cox steers a rowing boat, the helmsman's role on a small craft.

clue.text: Superior painting possibly including new organ

indicators.note: including means the outer word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: painting is one example of art

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters of organ

explanation.surface: A fine picture which happens to show a freshly built church instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like praise for the painting, but it is the definition, meaning haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in the sense of haughty and condescending, looking down on others.

clue.text: Having gun, journalist gets temporarily confined

parts.note: a gat is slang for a gun, from Gatling
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who is armed finds himself locked up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Gated is the school and college punishment of being kept in the grounds for a set period.

clue.text: Member arrives behind time to discharge parliamentary business

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
someone who arrives behind time is late

explanation.surface: An MP turns up late for the business of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing laws is the main business a parliament exists to carry out.

clue.text: Endless palaver about commander's centre of activity

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word is placed around the other piece
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a palaver is a fuss or commotion
OC stands for officer commanding

explanation.surface: Constant fuss surrounding the commanding officer's hub of operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commander' is the army abbreviation for officer commanding, not a rank in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is the central point where attention or activity gathers.

clue.text: Sort of acid remark initially disrupts play

indicators.note: disrupts means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: folic acid is a B vitamin

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter

explanation.surface: A caustic comment interrupts a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid remark' looks like one phrase; 'Sort of acid' is FOLIC, and 'remark initially' is R, put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to play about in a lively, light-hearted way.

clue.text: Birds crossing ends of lake: terrible place for a light boat

indicators.note: crossing means the birds stretch across the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: cocks are male birds

indicators.note: ends of means the first and last letters

parts.note: hell is the worst of places

explanation.surface: Birds flying over a lake that is a dreadful spot for a flimsy vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible place' reads as a judgement on the lake, but it is a separate piece meaning the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockleshell is a small, frail boat, named for its likeness to the shell.

clue.text: Troublemaker engineering several revolutions in Darjeeling?

definitions.meaning: someone who deliberately causes friction and discord
a spoon or stick that turns the tea round and round in the cup

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutions' suggests political upheaval but here it means circular motion; Darjeeling is a tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: one who stirs up trouble, and the implement that stirs a drink.

clue.text: First Quaker coming to revolutionary dance

clue.text: A course in Rome ultimately rivalling Cochin, perhaps

clue.text: Section of family in Gateshead retailing pork pies

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: Telling falsehoods, with retailing as recounting and pork pies as rhyming slang for untruths.

clue.text: Popular opinion, it's said, about gross lack of appreciation

explanation.walkthrough: ATTITUDE spoken aloud gives ATITUDE, one T lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingratitude is the failure to feel or show thanks for kindness received.

clue.text: Drink manufacturer's daughter, one showing less animation

stiller means more motionless

explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as whisky or gin by distillation.

clue.text: Bloke featured in song about northern country

clue.text: It's irritating, heading off backbite

clue.text: Work in non-poetic style Donne originally suggested

clue.text: Fiddler, perhaps, accidentally caught in a row?

clue.text: Starting with chicken, he replaces minder of animals

clue.text: Depressing game involving Stanley Gardner?

clue.text: Blustering woman? Without question
